Exam Date & Time: 26-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 2025 / JAN 2026  
  SUBJECT: PHY 1003/PHY_1003 APPLIED PHYSICS FOR ENGINEERS  
  APPLIED PHYSICS FOR ENGINEERS [PHY 1003]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                          Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Explain with a suitable diagram the construction and working principle of a semiconductor laser.             (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
1B)               An optic fibre of core refractive index 1.80 is to be cladded to ensure that the refracted light ray         (3)  
  grazes the interface. The optical fibre will contain light travelling within 10° of the fibre axis when it  
  is placed in air medium. What minimum refractive index is allowed for the cladding? If the same  
  optical fiber is placed in water medium (refractive index of water = 1.33), then find out the  
  acceptance angle and numerical aperture.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               What is modal dispersion? Which type of optical fibre can be used to remove this kind of                     (2)  
  dispersion?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2A)               Define (i) group speed and (ii) phase speed. Show that for a given non-relativistic quantum particle, (5)  
  the group speed of a wave packet is equal to the particle speed.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2B)               When a free electron scatters a 0.854 nm x-ray photon, the electron recoils with a speed of 1.48×            (3)  
  106 m/s. What is the resulting Compton shift in the photon's wavelength?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2C)                                                                                                                              (2)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3A)               Obtain the general solution to the Schrödinger equation for a particle of mass m in a finite potential       (5)  
  well of height U and length L. Mention the boundary conditions to solve this system. Sketch the  
  probability density for the lowest two energy states.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  Page #1

3B)          A student conducted a photoelectric effect experiment by shining light of various wavelengths onto       (3)  
  a metal surface. To stop the flow of photocurrent, the student applied a negative potential until the  
  current dropped to zero. The following readings were recorded. Are these readings valid? Provide  
  justification for your answer.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3C)          Increasing the mass of a particle enhances its tunneling probability for a fixed barrier. State          (2)  
  whether the given statement is True or False. Justify your answer.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4A)          Explain the phenomenon of single-particle interference with reference to the double-slit experiment. (5)  
  Illustrate your answer with suitable diagrams and discuss how this experiment demonstrates the  
  probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics and the principle of superposition.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
4B)          What are Bell states, and how do they illustrate the concept of quantum entanglement?                    (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)          The S gate changes the probability of measuring a qubit in the computational basis.                      (2)  
  State whether the given statement is True or False. Justify your answer.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)          Explain the working principles of the CNOT and CCNOT gates with the help of circuit diagrams and (5)  
  truth tables.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)          Prove the following identities:                                                                          (3)  
  $$a) = - = b) = - = c) = - =$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
